All new files are kebab-case and live under `src/` (so ESLint's `src/**/*.ts` rules apply) or `scripts/`. They depend on the existing library, never the other way around:

| `src/server.ts` | `createApp(store): http.Server` built on `node:http`. Reads the body, calls `route`, writes JSON, logs one line. | `routes.ts`, `node:http` |
| `src/main.ts` | Entry point. Creates `NoteStore`, listens on `PORT` (default 8081). | `server.ts` |
| `scripts/smoke.ts` | Black-box smoke against `SMOKE_URL` (default `http://localhost:8081`). Uses global `fetch`. | none |

`src/index.ts` (public library entry) is unchanged, so library consumers are unaffected. Node 24 runs `.ts` files directly (type stripping), which matches the existing `.ts` import style. New code uses only erasable TypeScript syntax: no enums and no parameter properties.

### ADR-1: Plain `node:http` edge over the existing Result-returning library
- **Status:** Accepted
- **Context:** The PRD forbids new runtime dependencies and requires reuse of `NoteStore` and `searchNotes`. The repository convention is that library functions never throw and return `Result<T>`, with HTTP status mapping only at the edge. ESLint enforces complexity ≤ 8 and max 40 lines per function on `src/`.
- **Decision:** Build the API on `node:http` with a hand-written router in `src/routes.ts`. Routing is a pure function from a normalised request to `{status, payload}`, so it is unit-testable without sockets. Status codes are assigned only in `routes.ts`/`server.ts`: `Result` errors map to 400 (`title required`, `term required`, invalid input) or 404 (`not found`).
